t: Hannibal took command of Carthage's army in Iberia at 26, attacked Rome's ally Saguntum and carried the Second Punic War into Italy by crossing the Alps in 218 BCE.
At Cannae in 216 BCE he surrounded and destroyed a larger Roman army, yet he could not take Rome, received little support from Carthage and was worn down over fifteen years in Italy.
Defeated at Zama in 202 BCE, he reformed Carthage's finances as suffete, was driven into exile by his enemies and by Rome, and took poison in Bithynia rather than be surrendered.
dyk: While wintering among the Gauls of northern Italy, Hannibal feared that tribesmen would try to assassinate him to win back Rome's favour, and took to altering his appearance with differently dyed wigs so that they would not recognise him.
ev: After the assassination of Hasdrubal, Hannibal is proclaimed commander-in-chief by the army in Iberia at the age of 26
He leaves New Carthage in late spring, crosses the Pyrenees, the Rhône and the Alps, and enters Italy
He destroys the army of the consul Gaius Flaminius in an ambush on the shore of Lake Trasimene
At Cannae he surrounds a Roman army, of which 50,000–70,000 are estimated killed or captured
He marches on Rome to draw off the besiegers of Capua, but the city falls to the Romans
After nearly 15 years in Italy he is recalled to Carthage to defend it against Scipio Africanus
Scipio defeats him at the Battle of Zama, the last major battle of the Second Punic War
Commanding a Seleucid fleet for Antiochus III, he is forced to retreat by the Rhodian navy at the Battle of Side

f.born: 247 BCE, most likely in Carthage; son of the Carthaginian general and statesman Hamilcar Barca, whose descendants are known as the Barcids
f.died: Between 183 and 181 BCE, at Libyssa in Bithynia; according to Cornelius Nepos and Livy he took poison when Roman soldiers surrounded the castle where he lived, though the precise year and cause are unknown
f.role: Officer under Hasdrubal the Fair in Hispania; commander-in-chief of the Carthaginian army in Iberia from 221 BCE; commander against Rome in the Second Punic War; suffete (chief magistrate) of Carthage after the war; military adviser to Antiochus III and commander for Prusias I of Bithynia
f.known: The oath never to be a friend of Rome; the crossing of the Alps with war elephants; the victories at the Trebia, Lake Trasimene and Cannae; fifteen years of war in Italy; the defeat at Zama by Scipio Africanus; financial and political reforms at Carthage; exile and death by poison
